Content: Students want to know which material will keep water in a glass bottle the warmest after `text(30 minutes)`. Their procedure and data are shown below.

:ibox:Students

• Wrap the `text(first)` bottle with `text(one)` layer of thin cotton cloth.
• Wrap the `text(second)` bottle with `text(one)` paper towel.

Content: A teacher performs a demonstration to show how different temperatures affect a magnet.
Before class, the teacher performs the following procedure to prepare for the demonstration.

:ibox:`1`. Gather `text(nine)` identical magnets, gloves, tongs, `text(three)` large bowls, and `text(186 grams)` (`text(g)`) of iron powder.

`2`. Fill each of the large bowls with `text(one-third)` of the iron powder.

`3`. Using gloves, place `text(three)` magnets in the freezer for `text(two hours)`.

`4`. Place `text(three)` magnets on the counter to keep the magnets at room temperature.
During class, the teacher uses the following procedure for the demonstration.

:ibox:`1`. Put on a pair of safety gloves.

`2`. Using tongs, place `text(three)` magnets in boiling water for `text(five minutes)`.

`3`. Using tongs, carefully remove the hot magnets from the boiling water and place them on a paper towel.

`4`. Using another paper towel, carefully dry the hot magnets.

`5`. Place the hot magnets in one bowl of iron powder for `text(five seconds)`.

`6`. Repeat step `5` with the cold magnets in the `text(second)` bowl of iron powder and then repeat with the room-temperature magnets in the `text(third)` bowl of iron powder.

`7`. Lift `text(each magnet)` out of the bowl of iron powder and measure the mass of the magnet and the iron powder. Record the mass, in `text(grams)`.
The teacher’s results are shown below.
:table:problems/FL25G5S/supps/FL25G5S-T9.json
Which statement is `bbtext(best)` supported by the evidence?

A.Choice: Cold magnets are as magnetic as hot magnets.

B.Choice: Hot magnets are less magnetic than cold magnets.

C.Choice: Room-temperature magnets are less magnetic than hot magnets.

D.Choice: Hot and cold magnets are more magnetic than room-temperature magnets.
